# FDG8066

> DO NOT throw exceptions from `Equals`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.9.1 Object.Equals.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1065
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Test profile: none, because CA1065 also reports property getters, static constructors and implicit conversion operators (FDG5031, FDG5054, FDG5092), and chapter 5 is off in the test profile; test fakes often throw NotImplementedException from stub getters, which CA1065 reports (probe with SDK 10.0.402). CA1065 reports an exception created directly in Equals(object) or IEquatable<T>.Equals (probe with SDK 10.0.402). Exceptions from methods that Equals calls, such as a null dereference of the argument, are not seen, so coverage is partial. Returning false changes no signature, but CA1065 has no code fix. CA1065 is shared with FDG5031, FDG5054, FDG5092, FDG8075, FDG8083 and FDG8101.

## From the book

Two objects should either be equal or not equal. So, for example, even if the argument passed to `Equals` is null, returning false is better than throwing an exception.
